syn: apt-file [options] search pattern ⏎ apt-file [options] show package

o.en: This option is useful if you search a package for a different architecture from the one installed on your system. It can be a comma-separated list for searching on multiple architectures.

Configuration File; Specify a configuration file to use. The program will read the default configuration file and then this configuration file. If configuration settings need to be set before the default configuration files are parsed specify a file with the APT_CONFIG environment variable.
Use contents of the given .deb archives(s) as patterns. Useful for searching for file conflicts with other packages. Implies -F.
Read patterns from the given file(s), one per line. Use - as filename for stdin. If no files are given, then the list will be read from stdin. This is much faster than invoking apt-file many times.

Only search indices from the listed origins (e.g. "Debian"). This filter matches against the name listed in the Origin field from the Release file. If set to '*', this filter will be disabled (mostly useful for overriding the setting in a configuration file) Alias of the APT config option: apt-file::Search-Filter::Origin

Only search indices from the listed suites or codenames (e.g. "unstable"). This filter matches against the name listed in the Codename and Suite fields from the Release file. This means that either "unstable" or "sid" will match Debian's unstable suite.
Do not expand search pattern with generic characters at pattern's start and end. This is default for show and list actions.

Only search indexes of the given name(s). If set to the special value ALL (case-sensitive), then all apt-file indices are searched. The name(s) must match one or more of the identifiers used in the APT configuration (minus leading "Contents-").
Ignore case when searching for pattern.
Only display package name; do not display file names.

This is a special-usage option useful for dealing with searches that produce a high number of matches (10 000+) or/and automated processing of results. Disable deduplication logic and immediately emit a result when a match is found.

Set a Configuration Option; This will set an arbitrary configuration option. The syntax is -o APT::Option=Value. -o and --option can be used multiple times to set different options. This option can be used to overwrite other command line options (e.g.
Match if the given search pattern is a substring of a path or package. This is default for search and find actions.
Treat pattern as a (perl) regular expression. See perlreref(1) for details. Without this option, pattern is treated as a literal string to search for. Be advised that this option can be rather slow.
